metadata.title: Vistara Polymers Cyber-Incident Investigation & Response Assessment
metadata.timezone_convention: All evidence IST except IIS artifacts (UTC + canonical header `Synthetic training data. IIS timestamps are UTC. Convert to IST by adding +05:30.`). Timestamp answers accepted in IST at minute precision (HH:MM) and, for IIS-derived items, the equivalent UTC value.
metadata.reconciliation_note: Agent 4.1 scoring reconciliation: equal pooling, Q-05-01 40-cell rule, evidence_selection explicit per task, Q-07-04 dwell tolerance 142h±2h

items.title: Triage & incident declaration
items.instructions: You are the Senior IR Analyst assigned to INC-2026-0417. Review the briefing ticket and the triggering SIEM alert in your workspace, then make your triage call.

sub_answers.question: Verdict for the triggering alert.
options: A - True security incident - declare and investigate
B - False positive - benign scanner noise

sub_answers.question: External IP implicated by the alert.

items.evidence_correlation: SIEM alert detail x ticket; (E-ALERT-002 cluster + E-EDR-008/E-NET-003 available in P1 disprove the false-positive option).

hints.text: Read the alert's full process lineage and destination, then check whether the dossier or ticket describes any sanctioned activity that matches it.

common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: The alert shows an encoded-PowerShell child of a scheduled task making an external 8443 connection from APP-PRD-01; no scanner job or benign process matches that lineage.

evidence_selection.rule: full points iff selection superset of required_set with zero incorrect IDs; half iff superset with <=2 incorrect; else 0

items.title: Reading the correlation cluster
items.instructions: Open the SIEM correlation view that followed the alert. Establish which hosts the incident touches and what the recurring outbound connections mean before you dig deeper.

sub_answers.question: Which hosts appear in the correlated cluster?
The ~30-minute small outbound connections 10.10.20.21 -> 185.220.101.47:8443 most likely indicate:
options: B - An active C2 beacon from APP-PRD-01

items.evidence_correlation: Cluster view x FW-01 beacon cadence x EDR schtasks artifact.

hints.text: Pull the underlying artifacts the cluster references rather than reading the cluster summary alone; compare the cadence and packet size of the 8443 traffic against known benign service patterns in the dossier.

common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: Neither appears in the cluster; ERP shows only a later single failed probe and DB a later read-only session.

evidence_selection.rule: full points iff selection superset of required_set with zero incorrect IDs; half iff superset with <=2 incorrect; else 0

items.title: Signal vs noise: the vulnerability scanner
items.instructions: While reviewing activity around the incident window you find vulnerability-scan-like behavior on 2026-09-04 09:15-11:02 and again 2026-09-08 02:00-03:47. Decide whether it belongs to the attack.

sub_answers.question: Select ALL facts that rule it out.
options: i - Source is 10.10.40.13, the registered VULN-01 scanner
ii - Jobs ran authenticated as svc_monitor with scanner job logs (VS-MAN-2026-0904 on-demand, VS-WK37-2026 scheduled)
iv - Plugin-based host enumeration with no follow-on exploitation
v - The Tuesday 02:00 schedule proves the 09-04 run was routine
vi - No attacker behavior is ever sourced from 10.10.40.13

items.evidence_correlation: Scanner source IP x asset inventory (VULN-01) x authenticated job headers VS-MAN-2026-0904 / VS-WK37-2026 x absence of follow-on exploitation (RH-01 rule-out).

hints.text: Trace the source IP in the asset inventory and read both job headers fully - note which job is on-demand and which is scheduled.

common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: Scan-like volume alone isn't hostile; the authenticated internal scanner with a named operator and no post-scan exploitation excludes it. (v) is wrong because the 09-04 run was on-demand, not the weekly schedule.

evidence_selection.rule: full points iff selection superset of required_set with zero incorrect IDs; half iff superset with <=2 incorrect; else 0

items.title: The exposure
items.instructions: Working from the perimeter evidence, identify exactly how the server came to be reachable for remote login from the internet and why that condition existed.

sub_answers.question: Which weakness made the initial access vector reachable?
options: A - W-01: a stale 2025 vendor-era FW-01 rule permitting TCP 3389 from any source to 203.0.113.10, never ticketed or removed
B - W-08: missing MFA on the VPN gateway
C - An unpatched IIS remote-code-execution vulnerability
D - W-06: the Plant VLAN -> FILE-PRD-01 SMB exception

sub_answers.question: Which policy/change-control failure explains its persistence?
options: A - CH-Policy-03: firewall rule added without a change ticket (grandfathered vendor session), conflicting with VP-Policy-05 vendor-access rules

items.evidence_correlation: FW-01 allow-rule visibility x 2025 vendor email (origin) x CH-Policy-03 / VP-Policy-05 policy gap.

hints.text: Look at which FW-01 rule allowed the inbound 3389 connections, then search the document store for how and when that rule was created.

common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: The attacker never used the VPN (see Q-02-02(d)); the exposure is the stale RDP rule.

evidence_selection.rule: full points iff selection superset of required_set with zero incorrect IDs; half iff superset with <=2 incorrect; else 0

items.title: Initial access determination
items.instructions: Determine the initial access event end-to-end: who probed, which account was broken, when exactly access was gained, and by which vector. Expect to correlate perimeter, authentication, and endpoint telemetry and to reject ambient noise.

sub_answers.question: External source IP of the focused campaign.
Initial access vector.
options: A - RDP brute force of svc_portal over internet-exposed TCP 3389
B - VPN login with stolen credentials (no MFA)
C - Web-shell upload as the first entry

sub_answers.question: Evidence-linked selection: select the artifacts that prove (a)-(d).

items.evidence_correlation: 4625 failure run w/ distinct substatus + 4624 Type 10 success 11:47 + DC-01 4776 NTLM validations (E-AUTH-001) x FW-01 session 11:47-12:20 (E-NET-005) x FW-01 scan/allow from same IP (E-NET-001) x interactive EDR session (E-EDR-001); VPN ruled out by E-AUTH-012 full-window summary; RH-07 ambient 3389 scanners rejected (distributed IPs, zero successes).

hints.text: Filter authentication events on WEB-PRD-01 by source IP and look for the failure burst followed by a Type 10 success; check the DC-01 4776 records in the same minute.
To eliminate the VPN hypothesis, read the full-window VPN session summary and compare source IPs.

common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: The shell upload (09-03 13:02) post-dates the 11:47 RDP success; no attacker IPs or svc_* logins appear in the full VPN window.

evidence_selection.rule: full points iff selection superset of required_set with zero incorrect IDs; half iff superset with <=2 incorrect; else 0 (candidate-facing expression: sub_answer (e))

items.title: The web shell
items.instructions: The attacker established a web-based way back into WEB-PRD-01. Locate it precisely and separate it from the historical shell fragment left over from the 2025 incident.

sub_answers.question: Full path of THIS incident's web shell.
Why is C:\inetpub\wwwroot\assets\old\upload_bak.aspx NOT this incident's shell?
options: A - It is a 2025-11-08 file quarantined per the IR-2025-011 note with no 2026 execution requests
C - It belongs to the marketing WordPress site
D - It has a valid digital signature

items.evidence_correlation: IIS POST 200 to upload.aspx then GET img.aspx?cmd=... x matching file-creation event; UTC->IST conversion required by artifact header; RH-05 rejected by 2025 timestamp + quarantine note + no 2026 hits.

hints.text: IIS logs are UTC - convert. Follow the 404 burst on /staging/ to the successful POST, then match the created file on disk; compare timestamps and paths against the 2025 quarantine note.

common_wrong_answer.answer: Naming upload_bak.aspx, or reporting 07:32 as IST
common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: upload_bak.aspx is the quarantined 2025 fragment (RH-05); IIS artifacts are UTC per the artifact header, so the IST upload time is 13:02.

items.title: Web/application weakness chain
items.instructions: Identify which validated weaknesses chained together to turn moderate web/application exposure into a foothold. Select from the weakness register (W-IDs).

sub_answers.question: Select ALL weaknesses in the initial-access/foothold chain.
options: W-02b - staging site + vendor upload page exposed without auth
W-03 - weak svc_portal password Portal@2024, documented

sub_answers.question: The documented internal source that published the brute-forced password.

items.evidence_correlation: FW-01 RDP rule (W-01) x exposed unauthenticated staging upload page (W-02b, E-WEB-002/003) x wiki-published svc_portal password (W-03, E-WIKI-001).

hints.text: Ask which weakness each attack step needed: reaching the host, getting the password, and regaining access without RDP.

common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: No-MFA is real but irrelevant; the VPN was never used by the attacker (E-AUTH-012).

items.title: Credential access chain
items.instructions: Trace how the attacker turned a service-account foothold on WEB-PRD-01 into a privileged domain credential. There were two credential recoveries - establish both and the failed attempt between them.

sub_answers.question: Account whose OLD password (RajKulk@2023) was recovered.
Result of the 15:12 authentication attempt to APP-PRD-01 with that old password.
File that yielded the CURRENT password.
The current password recovered there belongs to (username) and its value.

items.evidence_correlation: EDR dump + Credential Manager access x failed NTLM/4625 at 15:12 from 10.10.20.11 x findstr/type commands x passwords.txt content.

hints.text: Sequence the EDR events on WEB-PRD-01 after the RDP session: recon commands -> memory dump -> failed 4625 on APP-PRD-01 -> file search. The successful pivot one morning later tells you which recovery mattered.

common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: E-AUTH-002/003 record a bad-password failure; the old password was dead. The 09-04 success proves the current credential came from passwords.txt.

items.title: First lateral movement & privilege discovery
items.instructions: Establish the attacker's first successful hop off WEB-PRD-01 and what the subsequent domain enumeration revealed.

sub_answers.question: Destination host of the first successful lateral movement.
What did the attacker learn from net group / nltest / LDAP enumeration?
options: A - rajesh.kulkarni is a member of Domain Admins (migration leftover, W-04)
B - svc_portal is an Enterprise Admin
C - admin_legacy is the only Domain Admin

items.title: Identity persistence (rogue account)
items.instructions: The attacker created a durable identity for re-entry. Identify it, its privileges, its origin, and when it appeared.

sub_answers.question: Groups it was added to.
options: Remote Desktop Users (local on APP-PRD-01 & WEB-PRD-01)

sub_answers.question: Created by (account) and from which host.

items.evidence_correlation: DC-01 4720/4728/4732 events (creator + source workstation) x AD snapshot current membership x later svc_mon use (E-AUTH-007).

hints.text: On DC-01, look for 4720/4728/4732 events inside the incident window and check the creator and source workstation fields; confirm current membership in the AD snapshot.

common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: It is a pre-existing account (created 2019), never used by the attacker (14-month dormancy in E-AD-003).

items.title: Host persistence & C2 (scheduled task)
items.instructions: Characterize the persistence mechanism that survived on APP-PRD-01 and the channel it maintains. The mechanism's name is deliberately uninteresting - read what it DOES.
items.evidence_correlation: schtasks /create (EDR) x task XML (FS) x 30-min 8443 egress cadence (FW-01) x 4104 script-block decode (independent second source for the URL).

hints.text: Don't trust the task name - export the task XML, decode the -enc payload (the PowerShell Operational log gives you a second copy), and match the FW egress cadence.

common_wrong_answer.answer: Treating the task as legitimate Edge maintenance
common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: The action is encoded PowerShell calling an external IP:8443; legitimate Edge tasks don't do that.

evidence_selection.rule: full points iff selection superset of required_set with zero incorrect IDs; half iff superset with <=2 incorrect; else 0

items.title: Domain dominance (DCSync)
items.instructions: Determine how the attacker obtained domain-wide credential material, from where, against what, and the full consequence for credential hygiene during eradication.

sub_answers.question: Beyond user hashes, which domain credential was captured given the /all replication scope - forcing a DOUBLE reset during eradication.

items.evidence_correlation: 4662 directory-replication access on DC-01 from non-DC source (E-AUTH-006) x endpoint command line showing /all scope (E-EDR-009); krbtgt inference-by-design from the /all scope.

hints.text: Look for 4662 directory-replication access on DC-01 from a non-DC source, then read the endpoint telemetry in that session - the command line shows the scope.

common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: The /all DCSync scope captures every account's hash including krbtgt; missing krbtgt is the classic eradication failure (golden-ticket capability survives).

evidence_selection.rule: full points iff selection superset of required_set with zero incorrect IDs; half iff superset with <=2 incorrect; else 0

items.title: Persistence inventory (synthesis)
items.instructions: Before planning eradication, enumerate EVERY mechanism by which the attacker can regain or retain access. Select all that the evidence supports.

sub_answers.question: Select ALL attacker persistence mechanisms.
options: i - Rogue Domain Admin account svc_mon
ii - Scheduled task MicrosoftEdgeUpdateTaskMachineCore on APP-PRD-01
iii - Web shell img.aspx on WEB-PRD-01
iv - Golden ticket actively in use
vi - SSH key implanted on VPN-GW-01

sub_answers.question: Which capability does the attacker hold in reserve but has NOT exercised (so it needs eradication-side mitigation, not containment)?
options: A - Golden-ticket capability via stolen krbtgt hash

items.evidence_correlation: One identity artifact family (AD 4720/4728/4732) + one host artifact family (schtasks/task XML/beacon cadence) + one web artifact family (img.aspx); /all DCSync scope (E-EDR-009) proves reserve krbtgt capability.

hints.text: Count mechanisms by evidence type: one identity artifact family, one host artifact family, one web artifact family. Don't count capabilities never exercised as active mechanisms.

common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: The krbtgt hash was captured (EVT-020) but never used; it mandates the double krbtgt reset during eradication, not a fourth live mechanism.

evidence_selection.rule: full points iff selection superset of required_set with zero incorrect IDs; half iff superset with <=2 incorrect; else 0

items.title: Rogue account in action
items.instructions: Prove whether the attacker's created identity was actually used, and where.
items.evidence_correlation: FILE-PRD-01 4624 LogonType 10 for svc_mon (E-AUTH-007) x continuous RDP session 10:15-13:05 in EDR (E-EDR-015) x account provenance (E-AD-001/002).

hints.text: Search FILE-PRD-01 authentication events for the rogue account and confirm session continuity in EDR telemetry through the afternoon.

common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: E-AUTH-007 shows LogonType 10 and E-EDR-015 shows a continuous RDP session 10:15->13:05 spanning collection->exfil.

items.title: Collection & staging
items.instructions: Determine exactly what data the attacker gathered on FILE-PRD-01 and where it was staged. Distinguish collected data from data merely queried.

sub_answers.question: Select ALL data categories staged for theft.

items.evidence_correlation: dir/robocopy command lines x SMB file-open audit (E-SHARE-001) x Temp directory writes; DB read-only queries are answered by a different artifact set (queries != collection).

hints.text: Correlate the dir/robocopy command lines with SMB file-open audit and the Temp directory writes; the DB questions are answered by a different artifact set (read-only queries != collection).

common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: No bulk DB export or ntds.dit copy exists in evidence; DB activity was 5-row sampling only.

items.title: Exfiltration
items.instructions: Establish both exfiltration events, their volumes and destination, and explain an evidence-survivability gap the investigation must account for.

sub_answers.question: Match volume to each exfiltration event.
Why is the 09-03 exfil flow absent from NetFlow?
options: A - NetFlow retention is 7 days (W-09); the flow survives only in FW-01 connection logs + EDR
B - The attacker deleted the NetFlow records
D - The flow used DNS tunneling invisible to NetFlow

items.evidence_correlation: Archive creation times on each host x FW-01 outbound volume windows (exfil #1: E-NET-002/E-FS-002/E-EDR-002; exfil #2: E-NET-004/E-EDR-012/E-FS-006); NetFlow retention note (E-NET-006) + proxy negative record (E-PROXY-001) explain the 09-03 gap.

hints.text: Match archive creation times on each host against FW-01 outbound volume windows; read the NetFlow summary's retention note before assuming a missing flow means no traffic.

common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: No evidence of NetFlow tampering; the collector retains only 7 days and today is 09-09. staging.zip's 18 MB upload on 09-03 13:25 is a distinct first exfil of source code/config.

items.title: Scope discrimination: accessed vs compromised vs probed
items.instructions: Two systems brushed against the attack without being owned. Classify each correctly - this judgment drives containment scope.

sub_answers.question: DB-PRD-01 classification.
options: B - Accessed but not compromised (read-only enumeration: sys.databases + TOP-5 row samples, no bulk export)

sub_answers.question: ERP-APP-01 classification.
options: C - Probed only (single failed SMB connect 4625 at 09:33, no successful logon)

sub_answers.question: Which account authenticated to DB-PRD-01 during the enumeration.

items.evidence_correlation: SQL audit statement types/row counts (E-DB-001) x DB Windows-auth session (E-AUTH-008) x ERP single failed 4625 with no success (E-AUTH-009, E-EDR-013).

hints.text: Read the SQL audit for statement types and row counts, and the ERP security log for the exact event count - one failed SMB connect with no following success.

common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: Read-only Windows-auth queries from FILE-PRD-01, no persistence, no execution, no bulk export; containment of DB-PRD-01 would be over-scoping.

evidence_selection.rule: full points iff selection superset of required_set with zero incorrect IDs; half iff superset with <=2 incorrect; else 0

items.title: Breach scope: host classification table
items.instructions: Classify each listed system into exactly one column. This is the definitive blast-radius statement for the incident record.

sub_answers.question: Classify each of the 10 hosts into exactly one class: Compromised / Accessed but not compromised / Probed only / Benign-unrelated.
accepted_answers: Per-cell all-or-nothing: 40 cells (10 hosts x 4 classes) x 0.25 = 10 pts

items.evidence_correlation: Per-host: execution/credential-use proof = Compromised; successful logon without execution = Accessed; failed logon = Probed; no attacker telemetry = Benign. Sources: auth + EDR + FS artifacts per host family.

hints.text: For each host demand proof of execution or credential use: a successful logon alone is access, not compromise; a failed logon is a probe; no attacker telemetry at all is benign.

common_wrong_answer.answer: Compromised for DB-PRD-01 (over-scope) or missing DC-01's credential disclosure (under-scope)
common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: DB-PRD-01 shows read-only enumeration only; DC-01 is a full domain credential disclosure via DCSync. Misclassifying any Compromised host counts toward critical failure CF-3.

evidence_selection.rule: validation/authoring metadata only; the 40-cell table carries all 10 points; used for feedback and CF-3 evaluation

items.title: Breach scope: identities
items.instructions: Produce the identity blast radius - which accounts are compromised or attacker-controlled, and the domain-wide exposure verdict.

sub_answers.question: Select ALL compromised or attacker-controlled accounts.
Given the DCSync scope, must ALL domain credentials be treated as exposed?
admin_legacy's correct disposition.
options: B - Weak but unexploited - ~14 months without logon (last_logon ~2025-07); hygiene finding only

sub_answers.question: The two VPN users with odd-window activity are:
options: B - Both benign (Ahmedabad office IP 122.176.45.9; pranav.joshi orders match dealer POs; ananya.iyer covered by HR travel approval TRV-2026-0312)

items.evidence_correlation: Attacker-controlled use per account (auth/EDR/AD) x AD snapshot last-logon (admin_legacy ~14-month dormancy, RH-04) x VPN full-window summary + HR travel record (RH-02/RH-03 rule-outs).

hints.text: For each account ask: is there attacker-controlled use in evidence? Then check the AD snapshot's last-logon field and the VPN full-window summary plus the HR travel record.

common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: Dormant ~14 months (last_logon ~2025-07) and absent from every attack artifact; a hygiene finding only.

evidence_selection.rule: full points iff selection superset of required_set with zero incorrect IDs; half iff superset with <=2 incorrect; else 0

items.title: Timeline reconstruction
items.instructions: Drag the 11 shuffled incident milestones into chronological order. (Candidate sees event descriptions with dates hidden; ordering only.)
items.evidence_correlation: Milestone-to-artifact anchoring: recon (E-NET-001/E-WEB-002) -> access (E-AUTH-001) -> shell (E-WEB-003) -> credential (E-FS-003) -> pivot (E-AUTH-004) -> identity (E-AD-001) -> C2 (E-EDR-008) -> DCSync (E-AUTH-006) -> collection (E-AUTH-007) -> exfil (E-NET-004) -> detection (E-ALERT-001). Scored by Kendall-tau concordance x 10 pts, rounded to 0.5.

hints.text: Anchor the two exfil-relevant dates (09-03 vs 09-05) and the detection date, then place persistence strictly after the first successful pivot.

common_wrong_answer.answer: Placing the web shell before initial access
common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: The upload (13:02) rode the 11:47 RDP session's access.

evidence_selection.rule: no evidence-selection scoring on this task

items.title: ATT&CK mapping
items.instructions: Map each observed behavior to exactly one MITRE ATT&CK technique from the controlled list. Every behavior is evidence-backed; scoring is 1 pt per correct mapping.

sub_answers.question: Map behavior to technique: Procdump-style memory dump of w3wp.exe on WEB-PRD-01
Map behavior to technique: Credentials recovered from C:\Users\svc_portal\Documents\passwords.txt
Map behavior to technique: Interactive RDP session WEB-PRD-01 -> APP-PRD-01 using a legitimate account
Map behavior to technique: Intrusion conducted through legitimate accounts (svc_portal, rajesh.kulkarni, svc_mon)
Map behavior to technique: net group "Domain Admins" /domain, net group "Enterprise Admins" /domain
Map behavior to technique: nltest /dclist:vistara.local, net view from APP-PRD-01
Map behavior to technique: Creation of domain account svc_mon
Map behavior to technique: Adding svc_mon to Domain Admins / Remote Desktop Users
Map behavior to technique: schtasks /create of MicrosoftEdgeUpdateTaskMachineCore
Map behavior to technique: Encoded-PowerShell beacon every 30 minutes over HTTPS to 185.220.101.47:8443
Map behavior to technique: lsadump::dcsync /domain:vistara.local /all replication request from APP-PRD-01 to DC-01
Map behavior to technique: Bulk reads from S:\ and R:\ shares into C:\Windows\Temp\collect\
Map behavior to technique: Compress-Archive of the staging tree and the collect directory into zip archives
Map behavior to technique: HTTPS POST of archives to the attacker's 185.220.101.47:8443 /upload endpoint
Map behavior to technique: Clear-History, ConsoleHost_history.txt deletion, recycle-bin emptying on APP-PRD-01

items.evidence_correlation: Each behavior row is quoted from its evidence artifact; ambiguous pairs (T1041 vs T1567) resolved by the channel evidence actually shows - the same 8443 endpoint as the beacon.

hints.text: Match each behavior row to the evidence artifact quoted beside it; where two techniques look close (e.g., exfil-over-C2 vs exfil-over-web-service), prefer the channel the evidence actually shows - the same 8443 endpoint as the beacon.

common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: The exfil rode the existing C2 endpoint (185.220.101.47:8443), i.e., exfiltration over the C2 channel (T1041).

evidence_selection.rule: authoring/validation metadata; evidence selection is not scored (15 mappings x 1.0)

items.title: IOC consolidation
items.instructions: Assemble the defensible indicator set for blocking and threat-hunting. Include only indicators tied to THIS attacker; reject benign and historical look-alikes.

sub_answers.question: Highest-priority indicator to block at FW-01 immediately.

items.evidence_correlation: Attacker-attributability test per indicator: scanner (E-VULN-001/002), office-egress IP (E-AUTH-010/012), benign VPN users (E-AUTH-011/E-DOC-003), and the 2025 shell (E-FS-007/E-DOC-002) all fail it.

hints.text: An IOC must be attacker-attributable: test each candidate against its evidence - scanner, office-egress IP, and the 2025 shell all fail that test.

common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: Registered Ahmedabad office egress and the internal scanner; blocking them causes business harm.

evidence_selection.rule: full points iff selection superset of required_set with zero incorrect IDs; half iff superset with <=2 incorrect; else 0

items.title: Containment decision
items.instructions: It is 2026-09-09 ~10:00 IST; the attacker's beacon is live. Select the containment set to execute now. Over- and under-containment both cost points; the set must be evidence-driven.

sub_answers.question: Network action.
options: C - Block both attacker IPs AND take the DMZ offline

sub_answers.question: Web action.
options: A - Suspend the /staging/ site on WEB-PRD-01
B - Take the entire dealer portal offline

sub_answers.question: Primary rationale for isolating APP-PRD-01.
options: A - Host exhibits an active C2 beacon and holds attacker persistence
B - It is the oldest server
C - Policy requires isolating all servers
D - It is nearest to DC-01

items.evidence_correlation: Contain only proven-compromised/attacker-controlled assets (canon state per EVT-033 / E-RESP-001 / E-AD-004); dossier business context: DC-01 isolation would halt domain auth; ERP/payroll criticality.

hints.text: Contain what is proven compromised or attacker-controlled - no more (domain auth and payroll depend on the rest), no less (a beacon is still running).

common_wrong_answer.answer: Isolating DC-01 (overbroad), monitor-only (under-reactive), or disabling admin_legacy
common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: DC-01 isolation causes a domain-wide authentication outage; a live C2 demands the block; admin_legacy is not compromised.

evidence_selection.rule: full points iff selection superset of required_set with zero incorrect IDs; half iff superset with <=2 incorrect; else 0

items.title: Response lifecycle sequencing
items.instructions: Order the major response actions. One of these orderings destroys evidence and leaves persistence alive - identify the defensible sequence.

sub_answers.question: Order the 5 major response actions.
canonical_answer: Evidence preservation (snapshots, memory, SIEM export, chain of custody)
Eradication (remove persistence, close weaknesses, reset credentials)

items.evidence_correlation: IR-Policy-01 (dossier) + response-record conventions (E-RESP-001 -> E-RESP-004 ordering): preservation after urgent containment, before eradication.

hints.text: Urgent containment comes first; destructive cleanup must never precede preservation; you cannot validate a state you have not yet restored.

common_wrong_answer.why_wrong: Urgent containment stops the bleeding first; preservation immediately follows, before eradication.

evidence_selection.rule: no evidence-selection scoring on this task

items.title: Eradication plan
items.instructions: Select every action required to evict the attacker and close what let them in, then order the plan. "Restore from backup" alone is NOT eradication.

sub_answers.question: Select ALL required eradication actions.

scoring.dimension_note: Investigative 55% = D1+D2; response decisions 28% = D3+D4+D5; validation+reporting 17% = D6+D7. Final score = sum over dimensions of (earned/max x weight).

grading_formulas.single: All-or-nothing per sub-answer (single answer / single choice / yes-no / timestamp; accepted aliases per item).
grading_formulas.multi_select: earned = points_component x max(0, TP - FP) / |correct set|, rounded to nearest 0.5.
grading_formulas.classification_table: Per-cell all-or-nothing using the item's cell_count and cell_points fields: earned = correct_cells x cell_points (cell_count x cell_points = task points). Q-05-01: cell_count=40 (10 hosts x 4 classes), cell_points=0.25 -> 10 pts.
grading_formulas.ordered_sequence: Kendall-tau concordance: earned = points x concordant_pairs / total_pairs, rounded to nearest 0.5.
grading_formulas.equal_pooling: All scored answer components within a task are equally weighted: points per component = component pool / N. No custom per-component weights anywhere. Documented exception by design: Q-07-04 = 10 deterministic fields x 1.0 + 1 rubric-scored executive summary 5.0.
grading_formulas.evidence_linked: The 80/20 evidence rule applies to every evidence_linked task EXCEPT Q-05-01 (26 tasks flagged evidence_linked; 25 carry scored evidence selection). Evidence selection = 20% of task points (full 20% iff selected set superset of required set with zero incorrect IDs; half (10%) iff superset with <=2 incorrect; else 0); answer components share the remaining 80% equally (pool/N). Q-02-02 explicit split: (a)-(d) = 2.0 each (the 80% answer pool) and (e) = 2.0 under the tier rule ((e) IS the 20% evidence component; no additional rescale). Q-05-01 is exempt: 40 cells x 0.25 = 10 pts; its evidence requirement is validation/authoring metadata (feedback + CF-3 evaluation), earning no separate points.
grading_formulas.negative_marking: None on investigative items; decision items lose their own points only.

scoring.hint_policy: Max 2 hints per task. Hint penalty = hint_penalty points deducted from that task's earned score (floor 0). Hints never name the answer.
